edges.description: It demonstrates that losing Asxl2 does dysregulate histone marks and gene expression in vivo, which supports the chromatin node in kind. It does not model this disease: the phenotype it produces is haematological, the genotype is a deletion rather than a truncating allele, and the developmental features that define Shashi-Pena syndrome are not what the model was assessed for.
edges.limitations: Two mismatches, and the second is the important one. First, the readout is myeloid rather than neurodevelopmental. Second, a deletion models haploinsufficiency or null, whereas the human disease is caused by truncating variants whose transcripts escape nonsense-mediated decay and which are argued to act dominant-negatively - so the mouse may be testing a different molecular lesion, not merely a different tissue.

edges.description: The null mouse's glucose intolerance, insulin resistance and lipodystrophy is the observation that generated the metabolic prediction for this syndrome, and a human case has since matched it.
edges.limitations: The mouse phenotype and the human case are one-to-one: a single reported patient with type 2 diabetes. Fidelity is called MODERATE on the strength of the prediction having been met once, not on any systematic comparison. The metabolic characterisation is also cited here second-hand, from the case report rather than from the primary mouse metabolic study.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of Asxl2 leads to myeloid malignancies in mice.
evidence.snippet: ASXL2 is frequently mutated in acute myeloid leukaemia patients with t(8;21).

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis of Shashi-Pena Syndrome Caused by Chromosomal Rearrangement Using Nanopore Sequencing.
evidence.snippet: The aim of this study was to uncover the genetic cause of delayed psychomotor development and variable intellectual disability in a proband whose previous genetic analyses, including chromosome microarray and whole exome sequencing, had been negative.

nodes.description: The available Asxl2 mouse. It was made and characterised to study myeloid malignancy, and that is what it shows: increased long-term haematopoietic stem cells and granulocyte-macrophage progenitors, enhanced HSC self-renewal, dysregulated H3K27ac and H3K4me1/2, and a myelodysplastic-syndrome-like disease in transplant recipients. Separately, ASXL2-null mice are reported as glucose-intolerant, insulin-resistant and lipodystrophic.

Heterozygous truncating variants - nonsense and frameshift - in ASXL2. The defining series found six such variants in six unrelated probands, all de novo. Reported alleles since include p.Ser627Phefs*22 and further nonsense changes, and one family reached the same diagnosis through a balanced chromosomal rearrangement disrupting the gene rather than through a point variant.
The variant class matters. All three ASXL germline diseases are caused by truncating variants, not missense, which is the observation the dominant-negative and gain-of-function arguments in this gene family are built on.

evidence.reference_title: De Novo Truncating Variants in ASXL2 Are Associated with a Unique and Recognizable Clinical Phenotype.
evidence.snippet: In this study, we performed whole-exome sequencing in six unrelated probands with developmental delay, macrocephaly, and dysmorphic features. All six had de novo truncating variants in ASXL2.

evidence.reference_title: De Novo Truncating Variants in ASXL2 Are Associated with a Unique and Recognizable Clinical Phenotype.
evidence.snippet: We were also able to demonstrate with mRNA studies that these variants are likely to exert a dominant-negative effect, given that both alleles are expressed in blood and the mutated ASXL2 transcripts escape nonsense-mediated decay.

nodes.description:
ASXL proteins are the mammalian homologs of Drosophila Additional sex combs, which balances trithorax and Polycomb function, and they act as the scaffolding partner of the deubiquitinase BAP1 in the PR-DUB complex. The ASXL genes participate in body patterning during embryogenesis and encode proteins involved in epigenetic regulation and in assembling transcription factors at specific genomic loci.
This node is PROVISIONAL, and the reason is specific rather than routine. No chromatin abnormality has been measured in tissue from a person with Shashi-Pena syndrome. The chromatin account is inherited from what is known about ASXL1 and about the mouse, and a review of the family notes that the domains of ASXL proteins are partly distinct from Asx and that the roles and redundancies of the three members are not well understood - including whether truncating variants give loss of protein or a stable truncated protein with dominant-negative or gain-of-function properties.

nodes.description:
The route from a chromatin scaffold to macrocephaly, a specific facial gestalt, dental anomalies and variable intellectual disability is not traced. What can be said is that the phenotype is reproducible enough to be recognised clinically, and that it differs from its two paralogous neighbours in a consistent direction - overgrowth rather than growth restriction.
That direction is itself informative and is the reason this node is worth stating separately from the chromatin node: ASXL1 and ASXL3 truncations restrict growth, ASXL2 truncations do not, and one patient has been reported with marked postnatal overgrowth and only minor neurodevelopmental features, which has led to the suggestion that SHAPNS belongs among the overgrowth disorders with macrocephaly.

evidence.reference_title: De Novo Truncating Variants in ASXL2 Are Associated with a Unique and Recognizable Clinical Phenotype.
evidence.snippet: Although overlapping features with Bohring-Opitz and Bainbridge-Ropers syndromes exist, features that distinguish the ASXL2-associated condition from ASXL1- and ASXL3-related disorders are macrocephaly, absence of growth retardation, and more variability in the degree of intellectual disabilities.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Variability of Shashi-Pena Syndrome: A Novel ASXL2 Variant Associated with Overgrowth and Minor Neurodevelopmental Features.
evidence.snippet: This study supports the inclusion of SHAPNS in overgrowth disorders with macrocephaly, suggesting the analysis of the ASXL2 gene even in suspected subjects with normal bone age and confirms dental anomalies as a clinical feature of this syndrome.

nodes.description: Variable in a way that is clinically important: outcomes range from low-average intellectual ability to severe intellectual disability, and at least one reported patient has only minor neurodevelopmental features. This variability is itself a distinguishing feature against the ASXL1 and ASXL3 disorders.

evidence.snippet: Affected individuals can have variable developmental delay / intellectual disability, ranging from low-average intellectual abilities to severe intellectual disability.

nodes.description: Common, and one of the three features that distinguish this disorder from Bohring-Opitz and Bainbridge-Ropers syndrome. Macrosomia is also common, and growth retardation is characteristically absent.

evidence.snippet: Macrosomia and macrocephaly are also common.

nodes.description:
ASXL2 interacts with PPAR-gamma, and ASXL2-null mice are glucose-intolerant, insulin-resistant and lipodystrophic. That is a mouse-derived prediction about a human phenotype, and it is one of the few places in this entry where the prediction has been tested: an 8-year-old prepubertal boy with SHAPNS developed type 2 diabetes with dyslipidemia and fatty infiltration of the liver, in the absence of a family history.
It is graded PROVISIONAL because that is one patient. The source itself asks for further cases before treating the association as established, and the infantile hypoglycemia that is well documented in this syndrome is a different metabolic problem in the opposite direction, not obviously part of the same account.

evidence.reference_title: Prepubertal onset of type 2 diabetes in Shashi-Pena syndrome due to ASXL2 mutation.
evidence.snippet: ASXL2 null mice exhibit glucose intolerance, insulin resistance and lipodystrophy. The regulatory role of ASXL2 in glucose and lipid homeostasis occurs through its interaction with peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ), a gene implicated in the pathogenesis of type 2 diabetes on genome-wide association studies.
